elements.description: ลักษณะการวางพื้น SP บริเวณรอยตัดขาด 1:25 -- SP precast plank joint detail with 0.015m concrete topping and silicone building sealants
ลักษณะพื้น S ระดับสูงกว่าหลังคาน 1:25 -- slab level higher than beam, 0.40m offset, Ø9mm@0.20

warnings: This is the sheet that establishes the pile-count-per-footing rule for this house: F2=2 piles, F3=3 piles, F4=4 piles, F5=5 piles -- the pile count increases with footing size, not a fixed 2 per footing.

Footing plan dimensions (F2 1.10x0.55, F3 1.10x1.00, F4 1.10x1.10, F5 1.35x1.35) and their pile positions are dimensioned on this sheet's plan views; the section views confirm the 1.50m depth and 0.20m pedestal width for all four.
S0 (slab-on-grade, 0.10m thick) and CN (150x150mm column, 4-Ø12mm + Ø6@0.20 ties) are also detailed here -- CN's rebar matches the column schedule on S-02.
SP precast-plank joint detail and the 'slab higher than beam' detail are generic installation notes, not tied to a specific element_id on this sheet.

json.sheet_name: แปลนเสา คาน พื้น ชั้นล่าง, ชั้นบน
json.source_image: image/บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_04/บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_04_หน้า10.png
json.grid_source: บ้าน_ใหญ่_2ชั้น_04_หน้า00_gridline.json
warnings: This sheet is printed as TWO side-by-side plans on one sheet: 'แปลนเสา คาน พื้น ชั้นล่าง' (ground floor, left) and 'แปลนเสา คาน พื้น ชั้นบน' (upper floor, right), both at 1:100.0 Elements are recorded with a 'level' field ('F1'/'F2') rather than duplicated into two separate files, since the grid layout is identical on both floors and the only real difference is the stair-landing slab (S0) present on F1 but absent on F2.0 Both floors' beams are merged into one elements[] array with level noted per element.

The stair-landing slab marker 'S0' (printed twice, side by side, above row จ) appears only on the ground-floor plan — it is the small landing platform at the top of the exterior stair that rises from the carport/entrance area up to the main floor. It is ABSENT from the upper-floor plan, which is correct: the upper floor has no stair going up from it. Recorded as two separate S0 elements (one per marker instance) at grid_ref '~จ1' and '~จ2' on level F1 only.

The 'Bx (ข.พ.)' label (small beam, marked with a small circle symbol on the drawing) appears on the upper-floor plan only, at the left edge near grid 1 between rows จ and ค — this is the small beam supporting the stair opening edge on the upper floor. It does not appear on the ground-floor plan (the stair opening there is bounded by B3A/B3B instead). Recorded as element_type 'beam' with grid_ref '~จ1'/'~ค1' on level F2.

The 'CN' label (small square symbol, likely a concrete pedestal/short column at the stair landing edge) appears on the ground-floor plan only, at the left edge near grid 1 between rows ง and ค — same position as the Bx on the upper floor. Recorded as element_type 'column' at grid_ref '~ง1'/'~ค1' on level F1.

B7A (a short vertical beam, distinct from B7) appears on BOTH floors, running between rows ง and ค at the 0.95m offset line (between grid columns 1 and 2) — it is the beam framing the stair opening edge. Recorded as a single atomic segment per floor.
B5 (a short vertical beam) appears ONLY on the upper-floor plan, running between rows ค and ข at the 2-3 grid column line — it is absent from the ground-floor plan. Recorded only on level F2.

B4 (long vertical beam) appears on BOTH floors, running the full 4.00m span between rows ค and ข at both grid columns 1 and 3.0 On the ground floor it is the only beam in that row band besides B1; on the upper floor the same B4 position is flanked by B5 instead of the ground-floor's B1 cluster. Recorded as 2 segments per floor (one per column).

B1 appears in a dense cluster around the stair opening on both floors (vertical segments at the 0.95m and 1.30m offset lines, plus horizontal segments at rows ง and ค). On the ground floor there is also a B1 at row ข and another at row ก (the carport/entrance area). On the upper floor the B1 cluster is simpler (no row ข/ก B1s). All B1 segments recorded atomically.

The 0.20m and 0.50m offset dimensions near the left/right edges of the plan (at row ง/ค) are small beam stubs/offsets at the stair and room edges — not independently traced as separate beam elements since they appear to be part of the B3A/B3B/B1 edge framing already captured by the main grid-line beams.

pattern re-labelled 'etc_plan' -> 'beam_plan' on 2026-08-28, closing the schema section-1 plan-family split (the split created beam_plan/footing_plan/roof_frame_plan but every legacy file had been bulk-renamed to etc_plan, which section 1 defines as the residual 'not a beam plan, not a footing plan, not a roof-framing plan'). Decided from what the sheet DRAWS -- discipline plus the element_type mix, with the view's own title as tie-breaker -- never from the filename alone. Reason: 26 beam-family elements. Nothing else in this file changed.

The stair-landing slab marker 'S0' (printed twice, side by side, above row จ) appears only on the ground-floor plan — it is the small landing platform at the top of the exterior stair that rises from the carport/entrance area up to the main floor. It is ABSENT from the upper-floor plan, which is correct: the upper floor has no stair going up from it. Recorded as two separate S0 elements (one per marker instance) at grid_ref '~จ1' and '~จ2' on level F1 only.

The 'Bx (ข.พ.)' label (small beam, marked with a small circle symbol on the drawing) appears on the upper-floor plan only, at the left edge near grid 1 between rows จ and ค — this is the small beam supporting the stair opening edge on the upper floor. It does not appear on the ground-floor plan (the stair opening there is bounded by B3A/B3B instead). Recorded as element_type 'beam' with grid_ref '~จ1'/'~ค1' on level F2.

The 'CN' label (small square symbol, likely a concrete pedestal/short column at the stair landing edge) appears on the ground-floor plan only, at the left edge near grid 1 between rows ง and ค — same position as the Bx on the upper floor. Recorded as element_type 'column' at grid_ref '~ง1'/'~ค1' on level F1.

B7A (a short vertical beam, distinct from B7) appears on BOTH floors, running between rows ง and ค at the 0.95m offset line (between grid columns 1 and 2) — it is the beam framing the stair opening edge. Recorded as a single atomic segment per floor.
B5 (a short vertical beam) appears ONLY on the upper-floor plan, running between rows ค and ข at the 2-3 grid column line — it is absent from the ground-floor plan. Recorded only on level F2.

B4 (long vertical beam) appears on BOTH floors, running the full 4.00m span between rows ค and ข at both grid columns 1 and 3.0 On the ground floor it is the only beam in that row band besides B1; on the upper floor the same B4 position is flanked by B5 instead of the ground-floor's B1 cluster. Recorded as 2 segments per floor (one per column).

B1 appears in a dense cluster around the stair opening on both floors (vertical segments at the 0.95m and 1.30m offset lines, plus horizontal segments at rows ง and ค). On the ground floor there is also a B1 at row ข and another at row ก (the carport/entrance area). On the upper floor the B1 cluster is simpler (no row ข/ก B1s). All B1 segments recorded atomically.

The 0.20m and 0.50m offset dimensions near the left/right edges of the plan (at row ง/ค) are small beam stubs/offsets at the stair and room edges — not independently traced as separate beam elements since they appear to be part of the B3A/B3B/B1 edge framing already captured by the main grid-line beams.

pattern re-labelled 'etc_plan' -> 'beam_plan' on 2026-08-28, closing the schema section-1 plan-family split (the split created beam_plan/footing_plan/roof_frame_plan but every legacy file had been bulk-renamed to etc_plan, which section 1 defines as the residual 'not a beam plan, not a footing plan, not a roof-framing plan'). Decided from what the sheet DRAWS -- discipline plus the element_type mix, with the view's own title as tie-breaker -- never from the filename alone. Reason: 26 beam-family elements. Nothing else in this file changed.

warnings: Footing marks are printed as combined labels (e.g. 'C1,F4') — element_id is the footing mark (F4/F5/F6/F7/F8/F10), with the column mark (C1/C2) recorded in column_mark. This is the same convention used by house #2/#3's footing plans.
F10 appears twice on this sheet (row ง/ข, grid 2) — both are recorded as separate grid_refs, not merged into one count, since they are distinct physical footings at different rows.

F3 (row บ, grid 3) is drawn as a trapezoid/pedestal shape rather than a simple square/rectangle like the others — recorded as element_type 'footing' since it is a foundation element, but its exact shape (trapezoidal pedestal vs. footing) is not fully resolved from this plan view alone.
